theme: विविध यज्ञ / Many paths of sacrifice, all shaped by discipline and wisdom
context: Krishna broadens the meaning of sacrifice beyond symbolic ritual. He names several forms of yajña—material offering, austerity, yoga, study, and knowledge. The point is not that one ritual is superior in every circumstance, but that life can become a disciplined offering when it is rooted in self-restraint and truth-seeking.
contextHindi: श्री कृष्ण यज्ञ के अर्थ को केवल प्रतीकात्मक पूजा तक सीमित नहीं रखते। वे कई प्रकार के यज्ञ का उल्लेख करते हैं—द्रव्य यज्ञ, तप यज्ञ, योग यज्ञ, स्वाध्याय यज्ञ और ज्ञान यज्ञ। बात यह नहीं है कि हर स्थिति में एक ही विधि सर्वोत्तम है, बल्कि जीवन को अनुशासन, आत्मसंयम और सत्य-खोज से जुड़कर अर्पण बनाया जा सकता है।

wordByWord.meaning: sacrifices involving material offerings, resources, or practical service.

spokenHindi: यह श्लोक बताता है कि यज्ञ सिर्फ़ एक मंदिर की विधि नहीं है; जीवन का एक सामान्य, अनुशासित, शुद्ध रूप भी यज्ञ बन सकता है। द्रव्ययज्ञ में दान, सेवा और भौतिक अर्पण शामिल हैं; तपोयज्ञ में तप यानी संयमित और अनुशासित साधना को अर्पण माना गया है; योगयज्ञ में श्वास, ध्यान, वाणी और व्यवहार का संयम आता है; स्वाध्यायज्ञानयज्ञ में शास्त्रों का अध्ययन, चिंतन और विवेक को जीवन में उतारना है। 'यतयः संशितव्रताः' से तात्पर्य है ऐसे साधक जो अपने नियम को गंभीरता से धारण करते हैं। यह श्लोक यह नहीं कहता कि सब लोगों को एक ही साधना करनी चाहिए। यह बताता है कि सच्ची साधना कई रूपों में आ सकती है, अगर उसका केंद्र अहंकार को छोड़कर सत्य, अनुशासन और विवेक हो।
clearEnglish: Here Krishna widens the concept of sacrifice from external ritual to inward discipline. Some people offer resources, some offer austerity, some offer disciplined practice, and some offer learning and wisdom. The verse is not suggesting that all people should perform the same action in the same way. Rather, it implies that any sincere form of training can become a sacrificial act when it reduces ego, increases self-control, and steadies attention. A life of study, restraint, honesty, and service can be as significant as a temple rite. This is especially important in modern life, where people may feel spiritually inactive because they are not engaging in formal ritual. Krishna's teaching says that spiritual seriousness is not limited to one form; it is the quality of intention, discipline, and truthfulness. A person can become spiritually awake through disciplined speech, careful study, honest work, or patiently refined habits.

interpretationPerspectives.label: TEXT
interpretationPerspectives.explanation: The verse explicitly lists several yajñas: material offering, austerity, yoga practice, study, and knowledge. Krishna frames sacrifice as a range of disciplined practices rather than a single ritual template.

interpretationPerspectives.label: INFERENCE
interpretationPerspectives.explanation: The practical implication is that spiritual life is plural and personal. The Gita does not reduce holiness to one social role or one outward action; it values the inner quality of effort and sincerity.

practicalApplication.label: Study as offering
practicalApplication.text: Set aside ten minutes to read or reflect on one teaching that challenges your ego or habit. Treat the time as a quiet offering of attention, not just information gathering.

practicalApplication.label: One disciplined vow
practicalApplication.text: Choose one small vow for the day—no unnecessary criticism, no mindless scrolling after a certain hour, or one honest conversation—and keep it with steadiness rather than dramatic intensity.

reflectionQuestion: Which form of sacrifice in your life is most honest and sustainable: material service, discipline, study, or inner restraint?
reflectionQuestionHindi: आपके जीवन में कौन-सा यज्ञ सबसे ईमानदार और टिकाऊ है—द्रव्य-सेवा, अनुशासन, स्वाध्याय या अंतःसंयम?
